title: Helical Anomaly from Concurrent $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ Topology in an Acoustic Semimetal
authors: Hou-Yin Li, Hua-Shan Lai, Jian-Lan Xie, Xiao-Chen Sun, Yan-Feng Chen, Cheng He
abstract: Topological classification constitutes a cornerstone of modern condensed-matter physics. Historically, topological systems have been predominantly characterized by invariants confined to a single topological class, such as topological insulators with a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant and Weyl semimetals with an integer ($\mathbb{Z}$) topological charge. While such classification frameworks in principle permit gapless phases in which bulk and boundary degeneracies are protected by distinct invariants, this regime has received limited focused attention, as coordinating the requisite symmetries within a single band structure is highly nontrivial. Here, we realize such concurrent $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topology in a two-dimensional acoustic semimetal, revealing pseudospin-selective topological bulk modes arising from the interplay between these distinct invariants, termed helical anomaly bulk states (HABSs). Our lattice design exploits layer, sublattice, and gauge-staggered degrees of freedom, enabling modular control of effective time-reversal, chiral, and particle-hole symmetries. The resulting system exhibits bulk degeneracies protected by an integer $\mathbb{Z}$ invariant and Kramers-like boundary degeneracies protected by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant, forming twisted boundary arcs. Crucially, finite-size systems manifest helical or anti-helical edge states coexisting with HABSs, a distinctive signature absent in single-invariant topologies. Our results establish HABSs as a characteristic signature of concurrent topology and demonstrate a new regime where bulk and boundary invariants jointly govern topological transport beyond conventional single-class frameworks.
summary: This paper reports the realization of a novel topological regime in an acoustic semimetal where bulk and boundary properties are simultaneously protected by distinct $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants. By engineering the lattice symmetries, the authors demonstrate 'helical anomaly bulk states' (HABSs), establishing a new paradigm for understanding topological transport beyond conventional single-class theories.
main_problem: The paper investigates topological phases characterized by the concurrent presence of both $\mathbb{Z}$ (integer) and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants, a regime that is theoretically challenging to realize and study.
main_result: The authors realize and characterize 'helical anomaly bulk states' (HABSs) in a 2D acoustic semimetal, demonstrating that bulk and boundary degeneracies can be jointly governed by distinct topological invariants.
method: The research combines theoretical modeling (Hamiltonian construction, symmetry analysis) with advanced experimental techniques involving 3D printing and point-by-point sound pressure field measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-dimensional acoustic semimetal realized in a staggered lattice structure. The model utilizes engineered degrees of freedom (layer, sublattice, gauge-staggered) to control symmetries like time-reversal and particle-hole symmetry.
key_observables: Bulk degeneracies protected by $\mathbb{Z}$ invariants (Weyl points), boundary degeneracies protected by $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants (twisted boundary arcs), and the resulting pseudospin-selective HABSs.
important_parameters: The system's behavior is controlled by engineered symmetries and the interplay between the $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological invariants.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be effectively classified within the DIII symmetry class, and that the acoustic system can mimic electronic topological properties.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the band structure showing the coexistence of $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topology, visualizing HESs/anti-HESs, and confirming the existence of HABSs through measured and simulated dispersions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework of concurrent $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topology to detailing the physical realization in an acoustic semimetal, culminating in the experimental measurement and characterization of the novel HABS states.
why_interesting: The work extends topological physics beyond single-invariant descriptions, providing a concrete, experimentally verifiable platform (acoustic metamaterials) to study complex, multi-faceted topological invariants.
